newsitem.title: POLAND: EARLY ZLOTY SLIPS VS BASKET, SEEN STABLE.
newsitem.headline: EARLY ZLOTY SLIPS VS BASKET, SEEN STABLE.

text.p: The Polish zloty eased half a point against the currency basket in early trade on what dealers said was a single large exporter's order but stabilized at around minus 1.4 percent from parity, dealers said.

They said the zloty's downside was limited by expectations of central bank interventions, which have often occured at 1.5 percent below parity and by the bank's weekend statement it may further tighten its monetary policy to curb credit action.
"The central bank's announcement may stop the zloty from weakening," said Piotr Czyzewski, forex dealer at Bank ING.
A senior central bank official said in a Saturday paper deposit and credit rate rises in banks, which followed the National Bank of Poland's official rate rise on August 4, were not big enough.
He said that if banks did not raise their six-month deposit rates to 20-21 percent and credit rates accordingly, the central bank would have to further tighten its monetary policy.
Average six-month deposit rates in commercial banks after the NBP rate rise are currently between 17 and 20 percent.
The NBP has said that if the need arose it could raise banks' obligatory reserves and even impose credit limits.

At 0800 GMT the zloty was at 1.33/1.43 weaker than its currency basket against minus 1.47/1.57 at opening. It was at 3.4700/50 to the dollar and 1.9180/10 to the mark against opening's 3.4870/00 and 1.9200/30.
Some dealers said however, that even if the zloty fell strongly below the 1.5 percent support, the central bank would only intervene if it lost more than one percent in a day.
"The NBP is not likely to step in if the zloty falls or gains more than one percent during the day," a dealer at a foreign bank here said.

Polish T-bill yields are expected to again rise at today's 1.1 billion zlotys tender amid small demand after the central bank warned that it may further tighten monetary policy and dealers said the auction could push one-day deposit rates up.
On the money market one-day rates eased by close on one percent to 21.60/22.20 for O/N and 21.75/22.40 for T/N against Thursday's 22.45/23.00 and 21.80/22.00 percent respectively.
